citations.claim: first violation: total energy drifted to -292.1 from E0 ~26 during deep close encounter at distance 0.105
orbiter speed blew up to 18.47 at closest approach showing strong acceleration not resolved
energy already drifting one step before violation, -102 vs E0 26
two steps before, energy near 1.1, drift accelerating as separation shrinks from 0.70 to 0.42 to 0.105

counterfactual.change: reduced dt from 0.01356 to 0.001 with all else identical; finer timestep resolves the close encounter and removes energy violation

explanation: Two heavy bodies fall into a nearly head-on deep close encounter (separation 0.94 at step29 ->0.70 at step30 ->0.43 at step31 ->0.105 at step32, below softening 0.3). Leapfrog substepping grows only 11->12->13->16 substeps per outer step, so effective timestep stays too large versus the short dynamical time / huge acceleration (|potential| grows 1224->3809, kinetic 1250->3517). Energy drifts progressively 26.1->1.1->-102->-292, exceeding tolerance at step32. Momentum stays conserved, indicating a pure time-integration accuracy failure, not force asymmetry. Reducing dt alone removes the failure.
vision_note: Two blue bodies approach head-on and their separation shrinks from clearly visible to overlapping over steps 29 to 31. By step 32 they coincide into a single blob, indicating a deep close encounter.
